statement: A conditional transfer treated as a mortgage for the purpose of the Debt Conciliation Board's jurisdiction does not entail the consequence that title remains with the vendor (debtor).
supporting_quote: This argument was rightly rejected. It was held that a conditional transfer was treated as a mortgage only for purposes of the jurisdiction of the board and that such recognition by the board as mortgage did not entail the consequence that title remained with the vendor (debtor)

statement: A party claiming prescriptive title must demonstrate a clear separation of the land in question from the remainder of the property.
supporting_quote: There was no cogent evidence led to demonstrate a clear separation of Lot B, on the northern boundary, from the remainder of the land.

statement: A person who entered a land as a licensee cannot claim prescriptive title over the same piece of land without proving adverse possession independent of the licensor commencing from an overt act.
supporting_quote: A person who is let into occupation of property as a tenant or as a licensee must be deemed to continue to occupy on the footing on which he was admitted, until by some overt act he manifests his intention of occupying in another capacity. No secret act will avail to change the nature of his occupation.

statement: A court in a partition action may order the sale of the land in whole instead of partitioning the land, if it is inexpedient to allot divided portions due to the trivialness of the extent of the land.
supporting_quote: It is clear from this section that after trial, the District Judge can order the sale of the land in whole instead of partitioning the land.

statement: A party who holds legal title to property as a security for a debt is deemed to hold the legal title as a constructive trustee for the benefit of the transferor, subject to the discharge of the underlying financial obligation.
supporting_quote: Where it is established that the transfer was intended as security for a loan, the transferee is deemed to hold the legal title as a constructive trustee for the benefit of the transferor, subject to the discharge of the underlying financial obligation.

statement: An ultra vires administrative act can be challenged in two ways, including collateral challenge, but the question of collateral challenge does not arise in the circumstances of this case.
supporting_quote: Our attention was further invited to Administrative Law: Text and Materials [Beatson, Matthews and Elliot (eds.), 3rd ed., Oxford University Press, 2005, page 109] and Judicial Remedies in Public Law [Clive Lewis, 5 th ed. (Sweet and Maxwell South Asian Edition, 2017), page 187, paragraph 5-011] where the opportunity to impugn an invalid administrative act in collateral proceedings is indorsed.

statement: A constructive trust may be held to have been created if the Court can infer from the attendant circumstances that the owner did not intend to dispose of the beneficial interest in the property at the time the legal interest was transferred to the transferee.
supporting_quote: Where the Court can infer, as contemplated by section 83, from the “attendant circumstances”, namely the circumstances which precede or follow the transfer, that the owner did not intend to dispose of the beneficial interest in the property at the time the legal interest was transferred to the transferee, a constructive trust may be held to have been created.

statement: A third party cannot allege that the contract of sale is voidable on account of the doctrine of laesioenormis.
supporting_quote: A third party cannot allege that the contract of sale is voidable on account of the doctrine of laesioenormis.

statement: A party to a partition action who has been brought into substitute a deceased original defendant, who has failed and neglected to file a statement of claim or even a proxy despite notice/summons being served on such defendant, cannot be permitted to file fresh pleadings nearly 24 years after the institution of the action when the said action has reached the stage envisaged in section 184 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: I answer that question in the negative.

statement: A well-defined and identifiable course or track should have been adversely used by the owner of the dominant tenement for over ten years to acquire a right of way by prescription.
supporting_quote: It is a prerequisite to the acquisition of a right of way by prescription that a well-defined and identifiable course or track should have been adversely used by the owner of the dominant tenement for over ten years

statement: A co-owner can sue a trespasser to have their title to an undivided share declared.
supporting_quote: I am of the view that there is merit in the submissions of Dr. Coorey, the learned Senior Counsel for the Appellant, that the Appellant should be granted a declaratory order in relation to co-own the subject land.

statement: A co-owner may sue another co-owner of an adjoining land for the definition of boundaries without the participation of other co-owners.
supporting_quote: It is a well-established principle of law that a co-owner could sue a trespasser without the participation of other co-owners. (Hevawitrane v. Dangan Rubber Co., Ltd. 17 NLR 49; Arnolisa et al v. Dissan et al 4 NLR 163; Meera Lebbe Cassi Lebbe Marikkar v. Kalavilage Baba (1885) 7 S.C.C.) If a co-owner could sue a trespasser, in the same way a co-owner should be able to be sued without participation of other co-owners.

statement: A subsequent purchase of title by a party claiming prescription to the same land does not negate the prescriptive title acquired by such party to such land.
supporting_quote: any subsequent purchase of title by a party claiming prescription to the same land, does not negate the prescriptive title acquired by such party to such land.

statement: A party cannot acquire prescriptive title to a portion of a road if the final decree in a partition action has already wiped out all such rights.
supporting_quote: Nor can they claim any prescriptive rights to that portion because the Final Decree P4 wiped out all such rights, if they had any.

statement: A party to an action cannot raise the question of identification of the corpus for the first time before the High Court or in the Supreme Court, whether it is a partition case or a land case.
supporting_quote: The identification of the corpus is a question of fact or, at least, a mixed question of fact and law. It is not a pure question of law that can be raised for the first time on appeal.

statement: In a rei vindicatio action, the plaintiff need not prove identification of the land and the title to the land beyond reasonable doubt but on a balance of probability.
supporting_quote: This needs to be properly understood. This duty has satisfactorily been discharged by the plaintiff in this case.

statement: A party seeking to canvass an order entered ex parte against them must apply in the first instance to the court which made it.
supporting_quote: A party seeking to canvass an order entered ex parte against him must apply in the first instance to the court which made it. This is a rule of practice which has become deeply ingrained in our legal system.

statement: A valid marriage to which this Act applies shall be deemed at all times, whether before or on or after the date of the commencement of this Act, to have rendered, and to render, legitimate any child procreated by the parties prior to such marriage, whether or not such child was so procreated in adultery.
supporting_quote: It provides the following: “Legitimization of illegitimate children 3. A valid marriage to which this Act applies shall be deemed at all times, whether before or on or after the date of the commencement of this Act, to have rendered, and to render, legitimate any child procreated by the parties prior to such marriage, whether or not such child was so procreated in adultery: Provided, however, that where at any time before the date of the commencement of this Act any rights of any description whatsoever did not vest in the child of any marriage, but did in fact vest in any other person, by reason only of the fact that such child, having been procreated in adultery, was the illegitimate child of the parties, the subsequent legitimization of such child, by virtue of the operation of the preceding provisions of this section, shall not be deemed or construed (a) to have prejudiced or affected, or to prejudice or affect, in any manner, or to any extent, whatsoever the rights so vested, or such other person's claim or title to such rights; and (b) to have conferred, or to confer, on such child any claim or title to such rights.”

statement: An appellate court will not depart from the rule it has laid down that it will not over-rule the decision of the Court below on a question of fact in which the Judge has had the advantage of seeing the witnesses and observing their demeanour unless they find some governing fact which in relation to others has created a wrong impression.
supporting_quote: an appellate court- “will not depart from the rule it has laid down that it will not over-rule the decision of the Court below on a question of fact in which the Judge has had the advantage of seeing the witnesses and observing their demeanour unless they find some governing fact which in relation to others has created a wrong impression.”

statement: A party can acquire prescriptive title to land by possessing it as a separate land for several decades, independent of the title of the original owners.
supporting_quote: There is no doubt that the 4th Defendant has prescribed to Lots D and E by a title adverse to or independent of that of the Plaintiff and the 1st to 3rd Defendants as required by section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.

statement: A rei vindicatio action is not an action in rem but an action in personam.
supporting_quote: A rei vindicatio action is not an action in rem but an action in personam.

statement: A party cannot allege contrary things and be heard to assert the contrary.
supporting_quote: A person cannot say at one time that a transaction is valid and thereby obtain some advantage, to which he could only be entitled on the footing that it is valid, and then turn around and say it is void for the purpose of securing some other advantage. This is to approbate and reprobate the transaction.

statement: A plaintiff must disclose in the plaint why the cause of action is not barred by prescription as per section 44 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: if the cause of action arose beyond the period ordinarily allowed by any law for instituting the action, the plaint must show the ground upon which exemption from such law is claimed.

statement: For the defendant to prove 'adverse' possession, there should have been an intention by him to claim title to the land against its owner.
supporting_quote: There must be a corporeal occupation of land attended with a manifest intention to hold and continue it and when the intent plainly is to hold the land against the claim of all other persons, the possession is hostile or adverse to the rights of the true owner

statement: The correct shares should be allocated according to the actual shares transferred by the deeds, not the claimed shares.
supporting_quote: The correct shares should be as follows: 1st Plaintiff 7/288 2nd Plaintiff 7/288 1st Defendant 24/288 2nd Defendant 36/288 3rd Defendant 36/288 Unallotted 178/288 Total 288/288
